About

Academic background

I'm Seung Ho Jung. My master's research at Sungkyunkwan University's ECE department and Media System Laboratory (MSL) focuses on generative models, computer vision, and medical image analysis.

With 4 published papers, 1 accepted paper and 1 paper in progress, my work spans from medical vision models and representation learning to industrial applications. My background in software development supports the implementation of research ideas.

I also have more than 4 years of development experience, which includes several web development and architectural design of machine learning systems related with NNS.

ICISPC 2026July 12, 2026

Efficient Autoencoding with Quadtree-based Visual Transformer Encoder

Seung Ho Jung, Kyu Hoon Moon, Geonhyeok Lee, Jitae Shin

Accepted
At a glance & figure

Spend fewer image tokens on simple backgrounds, then restore a dense grid for reconstruction.

  1. 01Entropy-based quadtree patches
  2. 02Compact ViT encoding
  3. 03Mask-token grid restoration
Compute vs. dense ViT-B
17.5% less
Reconstruction PSNR
29.60 dB

STL-10 benchmark: 36.21 vs. 43.88 GFLOPS; PSNR 29.60 vs. 34.03 dB for dense ViT-B (Table 1, p. 8).

Trade-off: less computation, but lower reconstruction quality than the dense baseline and visible artifacts in some skipped regions.

Projects

Supporting engineering work

2024

Next-Generation Functional Desk

A wirelessly powered Raspberry Pi scanner that turns paper text into digital text and sends it to a computer.

Project details & figure
Hardware
6.78 MHz wireless power transfer supplies the Raspberry Pi through a battery pack. GPIO connects the scan button, illumination LEDs, and status indicator.
Software
A PyTorch CNN trained on the Stanford OCR Dataset recognizes text; Python handles capture, preprocessing, and Wi-Fi/TCP delivery to the host computer.
Team results
The four-person capstone poster reports 5 W output and 65% overall efficiency.

Waterbe Advertisement Tracking Website

A full-stack advertising dashboard for tracking campaigns, influencer activity, channel performance, and monthly client reports at Waterbe.

Project details & figure
Contribution
Contributed to frontend and backend development from November 2023 to May 2024, connecting client-facing dashboards with campaign data and reporting workflows.

2023

KNN Pest Disease Classifier

Image classification for agricultural pests and plant diseases, developed for NNS within a broader crop-diagnosis and pesticide recommendation project.

Project details & figure
Application
Identify agricultural pests and plant diseases from crop images as part of a broader service intended to connect farmers with relevant pesticide information.
Implementation
K-Nearest Neighbors classification using Python and OpenCV.
Project data
The project archive contains pest and disease photographs, banana-disease examples, Korean and English disease descriptions, symptom keywords, and crop-specific pesticide product lists.
Recommendation workflow
The accompanying design materials describe symptom-keyword extraction, manual keyword review, and linking disease terms to pesticide records. They also outline speech-to-text input and dialect-to-standard-Korean conversion for a chatbot; these are documented design goals rather than verified features of the KNN classifier.
PythonKNNOpenCV
2021

Korean Legal Text Classifier

A Korean NLP prototype for NNS that maps natural-language incident descriptions to major crime categories and specific offense labels.

Project details & figure
Application
Accepts a Korean incident description and returns matching major crime categories and offense subcategories. The taxonomy covers 19 major groups, including property, traffic, environmental, and labor-related offenses.
Data preparation
Selenium notebooks collect legal-document and Yonhap news text. CSV-based processing organizes articles by crime category; token-frequency comparisons and KR-WordRank experiments help identify category-specific keywords.
Classification
The Python prototype cleans Korean input, tokenizes it with soynlp LTokenizer, and matches tokens against curated CSV keyword dictionaries. Keyword rules can return multiple offense labels, with an other-category fallback when no match is found.
Dictionary maintenance
Supporting scripts add or remove category keywords in CSV dictionaries. Research notebooks also explore KoNLPy tokenizers and TF-IDF representations; the available inference script uses keyword matching.
